newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish far-right leader says he backs polls plan.
newsitem.headline: Turkish far-right leader says he backs polls plan.

text.p: A rightist Turkish leader with a key position in parliament said he would back Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's plans to resign and form a caretaker government to take the country to early elections.

"We will say 'yes' to this alternative so as to put the ballot box in front of the nation. We will support it because we want stability in Turkey," Anatolian news agency quoted far-right leader Mushin Yazicioglu as saying late on Monday.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, is expected to swap jobs with his coalition partner, Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, this week in a deal to call snap polls.
But the government is short of the majority it needs to get the power transfer and any election legislation through parliament.
The coalition has 274 deputies in the 550-seat assembly. Yazicioglu's Grand Unity Party has eight MPs.
President Suleyman Demirel, an avowed secularist, must also approve the power handover but he has not given any indications if he will allow the plan to go ahead.
